jazz_1925.csv.note: Ethel Waters recorded Dinah on October 20, 1925 for Columbia 487-D, billed with her Plantation Orchestra. It reached number 2 in 1926. Sweet Georgia Brown reached number 6 in 1925. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1926.csv.note: Ethel Waters recorded I'm Coming Virginia in September 1926. It reached number 10 in 1927.

jazz_1927.csv.note: East St. Louis Toodle-Oo was first recorded on November 29, 1926. The record that charted, Columbia 953, entered the pop list on July 30, 1927, during Ellington's first Cotton Club residency. Black and Tan Fantasy was recorded on April 7, 1927 and issued on Brunswick 3526. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1928.csv.note: The Mooche was recorded on October 1, 1928 and issued on OKeh 8623, with Baby Cox singing. It entered the pop list on December 29, 1928.

jazz_1929.csv.note: Am I Blue? and Birmingham Bertha were recorded on May 14, 1929 for Columbia 1837-D and sung in the film On with the Show!. Am I Blue? reached number 1. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1930.csv.note: Mood Indigo was issued on December 11, 1930 as Dreamy Blues, Brunswick 4952. The company changed the title to Mood Indigo in March 1931. Filed under the title it is known by, in the year the record came out.

jazz_1932.csv.note: It Don't Mean a Thing (If It Ain't Got That Swing) was recorded on February 2, 1932 for Brunswick 6265, with Ivie Anderson singing. On December 22, 1932 Ethel Waters recorded I Can't Give You Anything but Love with Duke Ellington and his orchestra, issued on Brunswick 6517. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1933.csv.note: Ethel Waters introduced Stormy Weather at the Cotton Club and recorded it on May 3, 1933 for Brunswick 6564. It reached number 1. Heat Wave, from Irving Berlin's As Thousands Cheer, was recorded on October 10, 1933. Underneath the Harlem Moon is her song in the 1933 short Rufus Jones for President. It was not issued as a 78. Sophisticated Lady was recorded on May 16, 1933 for Brunswick 6600. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1934.csv.note: Solitude was recorded on January 10, 1934 and issued on Victor 24755.

jazz_1935.csv.note: In a Sentimental Mood was recorded on April 30, 1935 and issued on Brunswick 7461.

jazz_1937.csv.note: The second edition of the Cotton Club Parade of 1937 billed Ethel Waters with Duke Ellington. Caravan, written by Juan Tizol, was recorded by Ellington's full orchestra on May 14, 1937. Barney Bigard and His Jazzopators, with Ellington at the piano, had made the first record of it on December 19, 1936.

jazz_1940.csv.note: Ko-Ko was recorded on March 6, 1940 and issued on Victor 26577. Taking a Chance on Love is from Cabin in the Sky, which opened on October 25, 1940. Waters recorded it on November 7, 1940 for Liberty Music Shop. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1941.csv.note: Take the A Train, written by Billy Strayhorn, was recorded on February 15, 1941 and issued on Victor 27380. Ethel Waters recorded Georgia on My Mind on August 15, 1939 with Eddie Mallory's orchestra. Bluebird B-11028 was released on January 31, 1941. Ray Charles's 1960 record stays in 1960. The order is a listening order, not a chart rank.

jazz_1953.csv.note: Satin Doll was recorded on April 6, 1953 at Ellington's first Capitol session and issued on Capitol 2458. It reached number 27. Billy Strayhorn finished the tune from an Ellington sketch. Johnny Mercer's lyric came later.
